QF.id: Introduction to AML, CFT and Proliferation Financing_8

question.text: The United States Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) of 1970 requires financial institutions to file reports if the daily aggregate of cash purchases exceeds:

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook records that the United States was one of the first nations to enact AML legislation, citing the Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) of 1970. Under the BSA, financial institutions must keep records of cash purchases of negotiable instruments and file reports if the daily aggregate of cash purchases exceeds $10,000. The Trap: Candidates sometimes blur the US BSA threshold ($10,000) with the Indian threshold (Rs. 10 lakh). Both use the figure "10", but the currencies and contexts differ. Note: Threshold-based reporting is a global AML design pattern; India's PML Rules apply a similar approach using the rupee Cash Transaction Report (CTR) thresholds.
